correctness.rationale: Exact conditional degree decomposition was reconstructed from independent edge variables and motif roles, yielding (1) for all n,h,k,p. Log R is strictly convex by a positive second-derivative sum and variance term, with endpoint divergence giving at most two roots. Regular-motif beta-shape maximum and falling-factorial expansion produce (2)–(3). For C4, the exact coefficient 3 binom(n,4) and cubic maximum 4/27 give n=6 sharp and the sparse covariance limit. Exact-rational exhaustive G(n,p) tests at n=4,5,6, three p values, and P4 irregular motif all passed. The finite checks are not offered as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Induced graphlet abundance and degree-frequency profiles are standard but dependent descriptors of random network structure. The theorem identifies a universal two-switch limit on their density-dependent covariance for all compatible nontrivial motifs, a sharp parameter comparison for regular motifs, and a sqrt(n) suppression band near the motif incident-edge fraction. The first realizable induced-C4/degree-2 double reversal at exactly n=6 and its sparse limit give a motivated structural boundary, not an arbitrary finite check; the general theorem does not follow merely from marginal data.
